chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-'Asemi narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi from Muhammad ibn Ali from Sharif ibn Sabiq from al-Fadl ibn Abi Qurrah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Mawali (non-Arab Muslims) came to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) and said, 'We complain to you against these Arabs. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to give us gifts equally with them, and he married Salman, Bilal, and Suhayb, but these [Arabs] refused us and said,
The Book of Livelihood from the Book of al-Kafi has concluded, and the Book of Marriage follows it. And all praise is to Allah, the Breaker of the Dawn.
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali advise the Mawali to do when Arabs excluded them from social and economic equality?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the socio-economic grievances of the Mawali (non-Arab converts) under Umayyad-era Arab dominance, where they faced systemic exclusion from equal stipends and marriage alliances. Imam Ali (peace be upon him) responded by encouraging economic self-reliance through trade, citing the Prophetic maxim that sustenance is largely derived from commerce, thereby offering a practical solution to their marginalization. This incident underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the Mawali's distinct status and the Prophet's guidance on economic empowerment as a means of social equity.
